	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.cells[r], 0, cols);
		}
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = this.cells[r][c];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.isSource()) {
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cannot be on the edge");
						}
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found");
						}
						Coordinate sourceCoord = new Coordinate(r, c);
						Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
						int[] offset = dir.getOffset();
						int targetRow = r + offset[0];
						int targetCol = c + offset[1];
						if (targetRow >= 0 && targetRow < rows && targetCol >= 0 && targetCol < cols) {
							Cell targetCell = this.cells[targetRow][targetCol];
							if (targetCell instanceof Wall) {
								throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source points into a wall");
							}
						}
						foundSource = termCell;
						sourceCell = termCell;
					} else if (termCell.isSink()) {
						if (!(r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be on the edge");
						}
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found");
						}
						Coordinate sinkCoord = new Coordinate(r, c);
						Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
						int[] offset = dir.getOffset();
						int targetRow = r + offset[0];
						int targetCol = c + offset[1];
						if (targetRow >= 0 && targetRow < rows && targetCol >= 0 && targetCol < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
						foundSink = termCell;
						sinkCell = termCell;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found");
		}
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[r][c];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
			FillableCell fillable = (FillableCell) targetCell;
			if (fillable.isOccupied()) {
				return false;
			}
			fillable.setPipe(p);
			return true;
		}
		return false;
	}

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		int row = coord.row;
		int col = coord.col;
		if (row < 0 || row >= rows || col < 0 || col >= cols) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate out of bounds");
		}
		Cell cell = cells[row][col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not fillable");
		}
		cells[row][col] = new FillableCell();
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.getCoordinate();
		queue.offer(start);
		visited.add(start);
		filledTiles.add(start);
		cells[start.row][start.col].setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			int currentDist = getDistanceFromSource(current);
			if (currentDist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (isValidCoordinate(neighbor) && !visited.contains(neighbor)) {
					Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
					if (!(neighborCell instanceof Wall)) {
						neighborCell.setFilled();
						filledTiles.add(neighbor);
						visited.add(neighbor);
						queue.offer(neighbor);
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.getCoordinate();
		queue.offer(start);
		visited.add(start);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.getCoordinate())) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			if (!(currentCell instanceof FillableCell || currentCell instanceof TerminationCell)) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighbor) || visited.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (neighborCell instanceof Wall) {
					continue;
				}
				if (canConnect(currentCell, neighborCell, dir)) {
					visited.add(neighbor);
					queue.offer(neighbor);
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the `Map` class does not have a constructor with the signature `Map(int, int)` or `Map(int, int, Cell[][])`. In the provided code, only constructors with parameters `(int, int, Cell[][])` are defined, but the code attempts to instantiate `Map` using `new Map(rows, cols)` which does not match any constructor.

**Explanation:**  
To fix this, you should add a constructor in the `Map` class that accepts only `rows` and `cols` parameters and initializes the `cells` array accordingly. This constructor will be used in tests or code that only specify the size without providing the cell array.

**Corrected `Map` class with the additional constructor:**

```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructor with only size parameters, initializes cells with FillableCell.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	// Existing constructors and methods...

}
```

**Note:**  
- This constructor initializes the `cells` array with `FillableCell` instances and sets up the source and sink cells as in the existing constructor.
- The existing constructor with `(int, int, Cell[][])` remains unchanged and can be used when a specific cell configuration is needed.

This fix aligns the class with the usage in tests and other code, resolving the compilation errors.

package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructs a map from a map string.
	 * <p>
	 * This is a convenience method for unit testing.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param rows     Number of rows.
	 * @param cols     Number of columns.
	 * @param cellsRep String representation of the map, with columns delimited by {@code '\n'}.
	 * @return A map with the cells set from {@code cellsRep}.
	 * @throws IllegalArgumentException If the map is incorrectly formatted.
	 */
	@NotNull
	static Map fromString(int rows, int cols, @NotNull String cellsRep) {
		var cells = Deserializer.parseString(rows, cols, cellsRep);

		return new Map(rows, cols, cells);
	}

	/**
	 * Tries to place a pipe at (row, col).
	 *
	 * @param coord Coordinate to place pipe at.
	 * @param pipe  Pipe to place in cell.
	 * @return {@code true} if the pipe is placed in the cell, {@code false} otherwise.
	 */
	public boolean tryPlacePipe(@NotNull final Coordinate coord, @NotNull final Pipe pipe) {
		return tryPlacePipe(coord.row, coord.col, pipe);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateStartCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			int row = rng.nextInt(rows);
			int col = rng.nextInt(cols);
			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			int dir = rng.nextInt(4);
			direction = Direction.values()[dir];

			if (row == 0 || row == rows - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			if (col == 0 || col == cols - 1) {
				continue;
			}
			switch (direction) {
			case UP:
				if (row <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case DOWN:
				if (row >= rows - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case LEFT:
				if (col <= 1) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			case RIGHT:
				if (col >= cols - 2) {
					continue;
				}
				break;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	@NotNull
	private TerminationCell.CreateInfo generateEndCellInfo() {
		Random rng = new Random();

		Coordinate coord;
		Direction direction;

		do {
			// false -> X-axis, true -> Y-axis
			boolean axisToClamp = rng.nextInt(2) == 1;
			int row = axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? rows - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(rows - 2) + 1;
			int col = !axisToClamp ? (rng.nextInt(2) == 1 ? cols - 1 : 0) : rng.nextInt(cols - 2) + 1;

			if (row == col) {
				continue;
			}

			coord = new Coordinate(row, col);

			if (axisToClamp) {
				if (row == 0) {
					direction = Direction.UP;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.DOWN;
				}
			} else {
				if (col == 0) {
					direction = Direction.LEFT;
				} else {
					direction = Direction.RIGHT;
				}
			}

			var adjacentCell = coord.add(direction.getOpposite().getOffset());
			if (adjacentCell.equals(sourceCell.coord)) {
				continue;
			}

			break;
		} while (true);

		return new TerminationCell.CreateInfo(coord, direction);
	}

	/**
	 * Displays the current map.
	 */
	public void display() {
		final int padLength = Integer.valueOf(rows - 1).toString().length();

		Runnable printColumns = () -> {
			System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			System.out.print(' ');
			for (int i = 0; i < cols - 2; ++i) {
				System.out.print((char) ('A' + i));
			}
			System.out.println();
		};

		printColumns.run();

		for (int i = 0; i < rows; ++i) {
			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(String.format("%1$" + padLength + "s", i));
			} else {
				System.out.print(StringUtils.createPadding(padLength, ' '));
			}

			Arrays.stream(cells[i]).forEachOrdered(elem -> System.out.print(elem.toSingleChar()));

			if (i != 0 && i != rows - 1) {
				System.out.print(i);
			}

			System.out.println();
		}

		printColumns.run();
	}

	public void fillBeginTile() {
		sourceCell.setFilled();
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	public void Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.cells[r], 0, cols);
		}
		TerminationCell foundSource = null;
		TerminationCell foundSink = null;
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				Cell cell = this.cells[r][c];
				if (cell instanceof TerminationCell) {
					TerminationCell termCell = (TerminationCell) cell;
					if (termCell.isSource()) {
						if (r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source cannot be on the edge");
						}
						if (foundSource != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple source cells found");
						}
						Coordinate sourceCoord = new Coordinate(r, c);
						Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
						int[] offset = dir.getOffset();
						int targetRow = r + offset[0];
						int targetCol = c + offset[1];
						if (targetRow >= 0 && targetRow < rows && targetCol >= 0 && targetCol < cols) {
							Cell targetCell = this.cells[targetRow][targetCol];
							if (targetCell instanceof Wall) {
								throw new IllegalArgumentException("Source points into a wall");
							}
						}
						foundSource = termCell;
						sourceCell = termCell;
					} else if (termCell.isSink()) {
						if (!(r == 0 || r == rows - 1 || c == 0 || c == cols - 1)) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must be on the edge");
						}
						if (foundSink != null) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Multiple sink cells found");
						}
						Coordinate sinkCoord = new Coordinate(r, c);
						Direction dir = termCell.getDirection();
						int[] offset = dir.getOffset();
						int targetRow = r + offset[0];
						int targetCol = c + offset[1];
						if (targetRow >= 0 && targetRow < rows && targetCol >= 0 && targetCol < cols) {
							throw new IllegalArgumentException("Sink must point outside the map");
						}
						foundSink = termCell;
						sinkCell = termCell;
					}
				}
			}
		}
		if (foundSource == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No source cell found");
		}
		if (foundSink == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("No sink cell found");
		}
	}

	boolean tryPlacePipe(int row, int col, Pipe p) {
		int r = row - 1;
		int c = col - 1;
		if (r < 0 || r >= rows || c < 0 || c >= cols) {
			return false;
		}
		Cell targetCell = cells[r][c];
		if (targetCell instanceof FillableCell) {
			FillableCell fillable = (FillableCell) targetCell;
			if (fillable.isOccupied()) {
				return false;
			}
			fillable.setPipe(p);
			return true;
		}
		return false;
	}

	public void undo(final Coordinate coord) {
		int row = coord.row;
		int col = coord.col;
		if (row < 0 || row >= rows || col < 0 || col >= cols) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Coordinate out of bounds");
		}
		Cell cell = cells[row][col];
		if (!(cell instanceof FillableCell)) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Cell is not fillable");
		}
		cells[row][col] = new FillableCell();
		filledTiles.remove(coord);
	}

	public void fillTiles(int distance) {
		if (sourceCell == null) {
			return;
		}
		filledTiles.clear();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.getCoordinate();
		queue.offer(start);
		visited.add(start);
		filledTiles.add(start);
		cells[start.row][start.col].setFilled();
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			int currentDist = getDistanceFromSource(current);
			if (currentDist >= distance) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (isValidCoordinate(neighbor) && !visited.contains(neighbor)) {
					Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
					if (!(neighborCell instanceof Wall)) {
						neighborCell.setFilled();
						filledTiles.add(neighbor);
						visited.add(neighbor);
						queue.offer(neighbor);
					}
				}
			}
		}
	}

	public boolean checkPath() {
		if (sourceCell == null || sinkCell == null) {
			return false;
		}
		Set<Coordinate> visited = new HashSet<>();
		Queue<Coordinate> queue = new LinkedList<>();
		Coordinate start = sourceCell.getCoordinate();
		queue.offer(start);
		visited.add(start);
		while (!queue.isEmpty()) {
			Coordinate current = queue.poll();
			if (current.equals(sinkCell.getCoordinate())) {
				return true;
			}
			Cell currentCell = cells[current.row][current.col];
			if (!(currentCell instanceof FillableCell || currentCell instanceof TerminationCell)) {
				continue;
			}
			for (Direction dir : Direction.values()) {
				Coordinate neighbor = current.add(dir.getOffset());
				if (!isValidCoordinate(neighbor) || visited.contains(neighbor)) {
					continue;
				}
				Cell neighborCell = cells[neighbor.row][neighbor.col];
				if (neighborCell instanceof Wall) {
					continue;
				}
				if (canConnect(currentCell, neighborCell, dir)) {
					visited.add(neighbor);
					queue.offer(neighbor);
				}
			}
		}
		return false;
	}
}

package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructor with only size parameters, initializes cells with FillableCell.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	// Existing constructors and methods...

}

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the code attempts to instantiate the Map class using constructors `Map(int, int)` and `Map(int, int, Cell[][])`, but these constructors are not defined in your current Map class. To fix this, you need to add these constructors to the Map class, ensuring they match the usage in your tests and other code.

Here's a correct implementation of the Map class with the necessary constructors:

```java
package game.map;

import game.map.cells.Cell;
import game.map.cells.FillableCell;
import game.map.cells.TerminationCell;
import game.map.cells.Wall;
import game.pipes.Pipe;
import io.Deserializer;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import util.Coordinate;
import util.Direction;
import util.StringUtils;

import java.util.*;

/**
 * Map of the game.
 */
public class Map {

	private final int rows;
	private final int cols;
	@NotNull
	final Cell[][] cells;

	private TerminationCell sourceCell;
	private TerminationCell sinkCell;

	@NotNull
	private final Set<Coordinate> filledTiles = new HashSet<>();
	private int prevFilledTiles = 0;
	private Integer prevFilledDistance;

	/**
	 * Constructor with only size parameters, initializes cells with FillableCell.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			for (int c = 0; c < cols; c++) {
				cells[r][c] = new FillableCell();
			}
		}
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sourceInfo = generateStartCellInfo();
		sourceCell = new TerminationCell(sourceInfo.coord, sourceInfo.direction);
		cells[sourceInfo.coord.row][sourceInfo.coord.col] = sourceCell;
		TerminationCell.CreateInfo sinkInfo = generateEndCellInfo();
		sinkCell = new TerminationCell(sinkInfo.coord, sinkInfo.direction);
		cells[sinkInfo.coord.row][sinkInfo.coord.col] = sinkCell;
	}

	/**
	 * Constructor with size and cell array.
	 */
	public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells) {
		this.rows = rows;
		this.cols = cols;
		this.cells = new Cell[rows][cols];
		for (int r = 0; r < rows; r++) {
			System.arraycopy(cells[r], 0, this.cells[r], 0, cols);
		}
		// Additional initialization if needed
	}

	// Existing methods...

}
```

**Explanation:**  
Adding the constructor `public Map(int rows, int cols, Cell[][] cells)` allows your tests and other code to instantiate Map objects with a predefined grid, resolving the compilation errors. The constructor copies the provided cell array into the Map's internal array, ensuring the map is correctly initialized for testing scenarios.

		VERTICAL(PipePatterns.Filled.VERTICAL, PipePatterns.Unfilled.VERTICAL),
		TOP_LEFT(PipePatterns.Filled.TOP_LEFT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.TOP_LEFT),
		TOP_RIGHT(PipePatterns.Filled.TOP_RIGHT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.TOP_RIGHT),
		BOTTOM_LEFT(PipePatterns.Filled.BOTTOM_LEFT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.BOTTOM_LEFT),
		BOTTOM_RIGHT(PipePatterns.Filled.BOTTOM_RIGHT, PipePatterns.Unfilled.BOTTOM_RIGHT),
		CROSS(PipePatterns.Filled.CROSS, PipePatterns.Unfilled.CROSS);

		final char filledChar;
		final char unfilledChar;

		Shape(char filled, char unfilled) {
			this.filledChar = filled;
			this.unfilledChar = unfilled;
		}

		char getCharByState(boolean isFilled) {
			return isFilled ? filledChar : unfilledChar;
		}
	}

	public void Pipe(Shape shape) {
		if (shape == null) {
			throw new IllegalArgumentException("Shape cannot be null");
		}
		this.shape = shape;
		this.filled = false;
	}

	public void setFilled() {
		this.filled = true;
	}

	public boolean getFilled() {
		return this.filled;
	}

	public Direction[] getConnections() {
		switch (this.shape) {
		case HORIZONTAL:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT };
		case VERTICAL:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN };
		case TOP_LEFT:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.LEFT };
		case TOP_RIGHT:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.RIGHT };
		case BOTTOM_LEFT:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT };
		case BOTTOM_RIGHT:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.DOWN, Direction.RIGHT };
		case CROSS:
			return new Direction[] { Direction.UP, Direction.DOWN, Direction.LEFT, Direction.RIGHT };
		default:
			throw new IllegalStateException("Unknown shape: " + this.shape);
		}
	}

	@Override
	public char toSingleChar() {
		return shape.getCharByState(filled);
	}
}

Response Text:---
The task is to implement the main game loop inside the `start()` method, allowing players to take turns, making moves until a winner is determined. The loop should:

- Retrieve the list of players from `configuration.getPlayers()`.
- Cycle through players in order, letting each make a move via `nextMove()`.
- Execute the move with `movePiece()`.
- Refresh the game display with `refreshOutput()`.
- Check for a winner after each move using `getWinner()`.
- Assign the winner when identified, and exit the loop.

Here's a complete implementation of the `start()` method:

```java
@Override
public Player start() {
    // reset all things
    Player winner = null;
    this.numMoves = 0;
    this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    this.currentPlayer = null;
    this.refreshOutput();

    ArrayList<Player> players = new ArrayList<>(configuration.getPlayers());
    int currentIndex = 0;

    while (true) {
        Player currentPlayer = players.get(currentIndex);
        this.currentPlayer = currentPlayer;

        // Get available moves for current player
        Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);

        // If no moves available, skip turn or handle accordingly (assuming game rules allow)
        if (availableMoves.length == 0) {
            // Optional: handle no moves scenario, e.g., skip or declare opponent winner
            // For simplicity, assume game continues
        } else {
            // Get the player's next move
            Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, availableMoves);

            // Make the move
            movePiece(move);

            // Update score if needed
            Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
            updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);

            // Refresh output
            refreshOutput();

            // Check for winner
            winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
            if (winner != null) {
                System.out.println();
                System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
                System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
                return winner;
            }

            // Increment move count
            this.numMoves++;
        }

        // Move to next player
        currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.size();
    }
}
```

**Explanation:**

- Initializes game state.
- Retrieves players from configuration.
- Loops infinitely, cycling through players.
- For each player:
  - Gets available moves.
  - Uses `nextMove()` to get the player's chosen move.
  - Executes the move with `movePiece()`.
  - Updates the player's score.
  - Refreshes the game display.
  - Checks for a winner with `getWinner()`.
- Exits when a winner is found, returning the winner.

This implementation ensures the game proceeds turn-by-turn, respecting the order in `Configuration#getPlayers()`, and terminates appropriately when a winner emerges.

@Override
public Player start() {
    // reset all things
    Player winner = null;
    this.numMoves = 0;
    this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
    this.currentPlayer = null;
    this.refreshOutput();

    ArrayList<Player> players = new ArrayList<>(configuration.getPlayers());
    int currentIndex = 0;

    while (true) {
        Player currentPlayer = players.get(currentIndex);
        this.currentPlayer = currentPlayer;

        // Get available moves for current player
        Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);

        // If no moves available, skip turn or handle accordingly (assuming game rules allow)
        if (availableMoves.length == 0) {
            // Optional: handle no moves scenario, e.g., skip or declare opponent winner
            // For simplicity, assume game continues
        } else {
            // Get the player's next move
            Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, availableMoves);

            // Make the move
            movePiece(move);

            // Update score if needed
            Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
            updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);

            // Refresh output
            refreshOutput();

            // Check for winner
            winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);

                System.out.println();
                System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
                System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
                return winner;
            }

            // Increment move count
            this.numMoves++;
        }

        // Move to next player
        currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.size();
    }

Response Text:---
The `updateScore` method calculates the Manhattan distance between the move's source and destination places and adds this value to the player's current score. The Manhattan distance is computed as the sum of the absolute differences of the x and y coordinates.

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
    Place source = move.source();
    Place destination = move.destination();
    int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
    int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
    player.setScore(newScore);
}
```

1. Retrieve the source and destination `Place` objects from the `Move`.
2. Get the `Piece` located at the source position.
3. Set the source position in the `board` array to `null` (since the piece is moving away).

```java
public void movePiece(Move move) {
    Place source = move.source();
    Place destination = move.destination();

    // Retrieve the piece at the source position
    Piece pieceToMove = board[source.x()][source.y()];

    // Remove the piece from the source position
    board[source.x()][source.y()] = null;

    // Place the piece at the destination position
    board[destination.x()][destination.y()] = pieceToMove;
}

	 * @param move the move to make

	public void movePiece(Move move) {

	 * Get all available moves of one player.
	 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
	 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
	 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
	 * @return an array of available moves

		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		ArrayList<Player> players = new ArrayList<>(configuration.getPlayers());
		int currentIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			Player currentPlayer = players.get(currentIndex);
			this.currentPlayer = currentPlayer;
			Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
			if (availableMoves.length == 0) {
			} else {
				Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
				movePiece(move);
				Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
				updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
				refreshOutput();
				winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
				if (winner != null) {
					System.out.println();
					System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
					System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
					return winner;
				}
				this.numMoves++;
			}
			currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.size();
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		int winningScore = 100;
		if (lastPlayer.getScore() >= winningScore) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
		player.setScore(newScore);
	}
}

public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> allMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];

                // Retrieve available moves for this piece

}

	}

	/**
	 * Get all available moves of one player.
	 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
	 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
	 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */
	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {

		return new Move[0];
	}

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		ArrayList<Player> players = new ArrayList<>(configuration.getPlayers());
		int currentIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			Player currentPlayer = players.get(currentIndex);
			this.currentPlayer = currentPlayer;
			Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
			if (availableMoves.length == 0) {
			} else {
				Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
				movePiece(move);
				Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
				updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
				refreshOutput();
				winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
				if (winner != null) {
					System.out.println();
					System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
					System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
					return winner;
				}
				this.numMoves++;
			}
			currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.size();
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		int winningScore = 100;
		if (lastPlayer.getScore() >= winningScore) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
		player.setScore(newScore);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		Piece pieceToMove = board[source.x()][source.y()];
		board[source.x()][source.y()] = null;
		board[destination.x()][destination.y()] = pieceToMove;
	}
}

1. Replace `move.source()` and `move.destination()` with the correct method names, which are probably `getSource()` and `getDestination()`.
2. Explicitly specify the type parameter when creating `ArrayList<Move>`.

Here's the corrected method:

```java
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> allMoves = new ArrayList<Move>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                // Retrieve available moves for this piece
                Move[] moves = piece.getAvailableMoves(this, new Place(x, y));
                for (Move move : moves) {
                    // Assuming getAvailableMoves already provides valid moves
                    allMoves.add(move);
                }
            }
        }
    }
    return allMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Knight;

public class JesonMor extends Game {
	public JesonMor(Configuration configuration) {
		super(configuration);
	}

	/**
	 * Get all available moves of one player.
	 * This method is called when it is the {@link Player}'s turn to make a move.
	 * It will iterate all {@link Piece}s belonging to the {@link Player} on board and obtain available moves of
	 * each of the {@link Piece}s through method {@link Piece#getAvailableMoves(Game, Place)} of each {@link Piece}.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure all {@link Move}s returned are valid.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param player the player whose available moves to get
	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */
	public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	@Override
	public Player start() {
		Player winner = null;
		this.numMoves = 0;
		this.board = configuration.getInitialBoard();
		this.currentPlayer = null;
		this.refreshOutput();
		ArrayList<Player> players = new ArrayList<>(configuration.getPlayers());
		int currentIndex = 0;
		while (true) {
			Player currentPlayer = players.get(currentIndex);
			this.currentPlayer = currentPlayer;
			Move[] availableMoves = getAvailableMoves(currentPlayer);
			if (availableMoves.length == 0) {
			} else {
				Move move = currentPlayer.nextMove(this, availableMoves);
				movePiece(move);
				Piece movedPiece = board[move.source().x()][move.source().y()];
				updateScore(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
				refreshOutput();
				winner = getWinner(currentPlayer, movedPiece, move);
				if (winner != null) {
					System.out.println();
					System.out.println("Congratulations! ");
					System.out.printf("Winner: %s%s%s\n", winner.getColor(), winner.getName(), Color.DEFAULT);
					return winner;
				}
				this.numMoves++;
			}
			currentIndex = (currentIndex + 1) % players.size();
		}
	}

	@Override
	public Player getWinner(Player lastPlayer, Piece lastPiece, Move lastMove) {
		int winningScore = 100;
		if (lastPlayer.getScore() >= winningScore) {
			return lastPlayer;
		}
		return null;
	}

	public void updateScore(Player player, Piece piece, Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		int distance = Math.abs(source.x() - destination.x()) + Math.abs(source.y() - destination.y());
		int newScore = player.getScore() + distance;
		player.setScore(newScore);
	}

	public void movePiece(Move move) {
		Place source = move.source();
		Place destination = move.destination();
		Piece pieceToMove = board[source.x()][source.y()];
		board[source.x()][source.y()] = null;
		board[destination.x()][destination.y()] = pieceToMove;
	}
}

public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> allMoves = new ArrayList<Move>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {
        for (int y = 0; y < board[x].length; y++) {
            Piece piece = board[x][y];
            if (piece != null && piece.getOwner().equals(player)) {
                // Retrieve available moves for this piece

public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Player player) {
    ArrayList<Move> allMoves = new ArrayList<Move>();
    for (int x = 0; x < board.length; x++) {

```java
public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
    // Create players: user player first to move first
    ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
    RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
    Player[] players = new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer };
    
    // Initialize configuration with players and protection moves
    Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, players, numMovesProtection);
    
    // Add initial pieces for user player
    Knight userKnight1 = new Knight(userPlayer);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(userKnight1, 0, 0);
    // Add more initial pieces for user as needed (example)
    // configuration.addInitialPiece(new Archer(userPlayer), 0, 1);
    
    // Add initial pieces for computer player
    Knight computerKnight1 = new Knight(computerPlayer);
    configuration.addInitialPiece(computerKnight1, size - 1, size - 1);
    // Add more initial pieces for computer as needed
    
    // Return the game instance
    return new JesonMor(configuration);
}

package assignment;

import assignment.piece.Archer;

import assignment.protocol.Player;

public class Main {
	/**
	 * Create and initialize a game.
	 * Student should first construct a {@link Configuration} object with two players.
	 * Then add initial pieces to gameboard in the {@link Configuration} object.
	 * After that, use this {@link Configuration} object to construct a {@link JesonMor} game object
	 * This method should return the created {@link JesonMor} object.
	 * <p>
	 * The initialized gameboard should comply to the requirements of the assignment.
	 * The user player should be put
	 * first in the player array in the configuration and user player should moves first.
	 *
	 * <strong>Attention: The code in this method is only an example of using {@link Configuration} to initialize
	 * gameboard, Students should remove them and implement on their own.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param size               size of gameboard
	 * @param numMovesProtection number of moves with capture protection
	 * @return the game object
	 */
	public static Game createGame(int size, int numMovesProtection) {
		// TODO student implementation
		// The following lines are example of constructing a game object, you may modify them as you wish.
		ConsolePlayer userPlayer = new ConsolePlayer("UserPlayer");
		RandomPlayer computerPlayer = new RandomPlayer("ComputerPlayer");
		// we give
		Configuration configuration = new Configuration(size, new Player[] { userPlayer, computerPlayer },
				numMovesProtection);
		Knight knight1 = new Knight(userPlayer);
		Knight knight2 = new Knight(computerPlayer);
		// put knight1 at place(0,0) on the gameboard
		configuration.addInitialPiece(knight1, 0, 0);
		// put knight2 at place(1,0) on the gameboard
		configuration.addInitialPiece(knight2, 1, 0);
		return new JesonMor(configuration);
	}

	public static void main(String[] args) {
		var helper = "two integer arguments are required specifying size of gameboard and number of moves with capturing protection ";

			throw new IllegalArgumentException(helper);
		}

**Complete method implementation:**

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> validMoves = new ArrayList<>();
    int[][] moveOffsets = {
        {2, 1}, {1, 2}, {-1, 2}, {-2, 1},
        {-2, -1}, {-1, -2}, {1, -2}, {2, -1}
    };

    for (int[] offset : moveOffsets) {
        int newRow = source.getRow() + offset[0];
        int newCol = source.getCol() + offset[1];
        Place targetPlace = new Place(newRow, newCol);

        Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
            validMoves.add(move);
        }
    }

    return validMoves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

- Iterates over all 8 possible knight move offsets.
- Creates a new `Place` for each potential move.
- Constructs a `Move` object from the source to the target place.
- Validates each move with `validateMove`.
- Collects all valid moves into a list and returns them as an array.

This should ensure all valid moves are correctly identified according to game rules.

 *

 */

	 * @param game   the game object

	 * @return an array of available moves
	 */

		// TODO student implementation
		return new Move[0];
	}

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new KnightMoveRule(),
				new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}
}

Response Text:---
The task is to implement the `getAvailableMoves` method for the `Archer` class, which moves similarly to a cannon in Xiangqi (Chinese chess). The Archer can move any number of empty squares along ranks or files, but to capture, it must "jump" over exactly one piece (the "screen") and land on an opponent's piece.

**Approach:**

1. Determine the current position (row, col) from `source`.
2. For each of the four directions (up, down, left, right):
   - Move step-by-step until hitting the boundary or an occupied square.
   - If no piece is encountered, the move is valid (empty square).
   - If a piece is encountered:
     - Continue moving in the same direction to find a potential capture move:
       - Skip the first piece (the "screen").
       - If the next piece encountered is an opponent's piece, it's a valid capture move.
3. Collect all valid moves in a list and return as an array.

Below is the complete implementation:

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    int row = source.getRow();
    int col = source.getCol();
    int maxRow = game.getBoard().getNumRows();
    int maxCol = game.getBoard().getNumCols();

    // Directions: up, down, left, right
    int[][] directions = { {-1, 0}, {1, 0}, {0, -1}, {0, 1} };

    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int r = row + dir[0];
        int c = col + dir[1];

        boolean screenFound = false;

        // Traverse in the current direction
        while (r >= 0 && r < maxRow && c >= 0 && c < maxCol) {
            Place targetPlace = new Place(r, c);
            Piece targetPiece = game.getBoard().getPieceAt(targetPlace);

            if (!screenFound) {
                // Looking for the first piece to act as a screen
                if (targetPiece != null) {
                    // Found a screen, now look for capture beyond
                    screenFound = true;
                }
                // If empty, can move there
                else {
                    Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                    if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                        moves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            } else {
                // After screen is found, look for opponent's piece to capture
                if (targetPiece != null) {
                    if (targetPiece.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                        // Valid capture move
                        Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            moves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                    // Whether captured or not, stop in this direction
                    break;
                } else {
                    // Empty square beyond the screen, cannot move here
                    // Continue searching for a capture
                }
            }
            r += dir[0];
            c += dir[1];
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

**Explanation:**

- The method iterates over four directions.
- It first moves along the direction until it finds a piece (the "screen").
- After finding the screen, it continues in the same direction to find an opponent's piece to capture.
- All valid moves are validated with `validateMove` before adding.
- The method returns all valid moves as an array.

This implementation ensures all moves adhere to the rules of the Archer's movement and captures, considering boundary cases and game rules.

	}

	private boolean validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return false;
			}
		}
		return true;
	}
}

The compilation errors indicate that the `Place` class does not have `getRow()` and `getCol()` methods, and the `Game` class does not have a `getBoard()` method. To fix this, you should use the appropriate methods provided by these classes to access the position and the game board.

Assuming the `Place` class has `getRow()` and `getCol()` methods, and the `Game` class provides a way to access the board (e.g., via `getBoard()`), but since the errors suggest these methods are missing, you should use the existing methods or fields.

If `Place` has public fields `row` and `col`, access them directly. If `Game` has a method `getBoard()` that returns an object with `getNumRows()`, `getNumCols()`, and `getPieceAt(Place)` methods, then the code should be correct if these methods exist.

**Proposed fixed method:**

```java
@Override
public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {
    ArrayList<Move> moves = new ArrayList<>();
    int row = source.row; // assuming 'row' is a public field
    int col = source.col; // assuming 'col' is a public field
    int maxRow = game.getBoard().getNumRows();
    int maxCol = game.getBoard().getNumCols();

    // Directions: up, down, left, right
    int[][] directions = { {-1, 0}, {1, 0}, {0, -1}, {0, 1} };

    for (int[] dir : directions) {
        int r = row + dir[0];
        int c = col + dir[1];

        boolean screenFound = false;

        // Traverse in the current direction
        while (r >= 0 && r < maxRow && c >= 0 && c < maxCol) {
            Place targetPlace = new Place(r, c);
            Piece targetPiece = game.getBoard().getPieceAt(targetPlace);

            if (!screenFound) {
                // Looking for the first piece to act as a screen
                if (targetPiece != null) {
                    // Found a screen, now look for capture beyond
                    screenFound = true;
                }
                // If empty, can move there
                else {
                    Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                    if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                        moves.add(move);
                    }
                }
            } else {
                // After screen is found, look for opponent's piece to capture
                if (targetPiece != null) {
                    if (targetPiece.getPlayer() != this.getPlayer()) {
                        // Valid capture move
                        Move move = new Move(source, targetPlace);
                        if (validateMove(game, move)) {
                            moves.add(move);
                        }
                    }
                    // Whether captured or not, stop in this direction
                    break;
                } else {
                    // Empty square beyond the screen, continue searching
                }
            }
            r += dir[0];
            c += dir[1];
        }
    }

    return moves.toArray(new Move[0]);
}
```

public Move[] getAvailableMoves(Game game, Place source) {

    int row = source.getRow();
    int col = source.getCol();
    int maxRow = game.getBoard().getNumRows();
    int maxCol = game.getBoard().getNumCols();

    int[][] directions = { {-1, 0}, {1, 0}, {0, -1}, {0, 1} };

    for (int[] dir : directions) {

        int c = col + dir[1];

Response Text:---
The `validate` method should check whether the move for an Archer piece follows the movement rules similar to a cannon in Chinese chess. Specifically, an Archer can move any number of empty squares along a straight line (horizontal or vertical), but to capture, it must jump over exactly one piece (the "screen") and land on an opponent's piece.

Here's a complete implementation of the `validate` method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    int srcRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int srcCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int destRow = move.getDestination().getRow();
    int destCol = move.getDestination().getCol();

    // Check if move is along a straight line
    if (srcRow != destRow && srcCol != destCol) {
        return false; // Not a straight line move
    }

    int countPiecesBetween = 0;

    if (srcRow == destRow) {
        // Horizontal move
        int startCol = Math.min(srcCol, destCol) + 1;
        int endCol = Math.max(srcCol, destCol);
        for (int col = startCol; col < endCol; col++) {
            if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().withCol(col)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Vertical move
        int startRow = Math.min(srcRow, destRow) + 1;
        int endRow = Math.max(srcRow, destRow);
        for (int row = startRow; row < endRow; row++) {
            if (game.getPiece(move.getSource().withRow(row)) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    }

    // Destination piece
    boolean isDestinationOccupied = game.getPiece(move.getDestination()) != null;

    if (isDestinationOccupied) {
        // Capture move: must jump over exactly one piece
        return countPiecesBetween == 1;
    } else {
        // Normal move: path must be clear
        return countPiecesBetween == 0;
    }
}
```

**Explanation:**
- Checks if the move is along a straight line.
- Counts the number of pieces between source and destination.
- For a capture, exactly one piece must be between source and destination.
- For a normal move, no pieces should be between source and destination.

This implementation ensures the Archer's movement rules are correctly validated.

The compilation errors indicate that the `Place` class (used for move source and destination) does not have `getRow()`, `getCol()`, `withRow()`, or `withCol()` methods. To fix this, you should access the position information via the `getPosition()` method (or similar), then retrieve row and column from that position object, assuming it provides `getRow()` and `getCol()` methods. Also, to create new position objects for iteration, use the appropriate constructor or factory method provided by the `Place` class.

Here's the corrected method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    int srcRow = move.getSource().getPosition().getRow();
    int srcCol = move.getSource().getPosition().getCol();
    int destRow = move.getDestination().getPosition().getRow();
    int destCol = move.getDestination().getPosition().getCol();

    // Check if move is along a straight line
    if (srcRow != destRow && srcCol != destCol) {
        return false; // Not a straight line move
    }

    int countPiecesBetween = 0;

    if (srcRow == destRow) {
        // Horizontal move
        int startCol = Math.min(srcCol, destCol) + 1;
        int endCol = Math.max(srcCol, destCol);
        for (int col = startCol; col < endCol; col++) {
            Place position = move.getSource().withCol(col);
            if (game.getPiece(position) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Vertical move
        int startRow = Math.min(srcRow, destRow) + 1;
        int endRow = Math.max(srcRow, destRow);
        for (int row = startRow; row < endRow; row++) {
            Place position = move.getSource().withRow(row);
            if (game.getPiece(position) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    }

    boolean isDestinationOccupied = game.getPiece(move.getDestination()) != null;

    if (isDestinationOccupied) {
        // Capture move: must jump over exactly one piece
        return countPiecesBetween == 1;
    } else {
        // Normal move: path must be clear
        return countPiecesBetween == 0;
    }
}

- `Place` does not have `withRow()` or `withCol()` methods.

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Archer)) {
        return true;
    }

    int srcRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int srcCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int destRow = move.getDestination().getRow();
    int destCol = move.getDestination().getCol();

    // Check if move is along a straight line
    if (srcRow != destRow && srcCol != destCol) {
        return false; // Not a straight line move
    }

    int countPiecesBetween = 0;

    if (srcRow == destRow) {
        // Horizontal move
        int startCol = Math.min(srcCol, destCol) + 1;
        int endCol = Math.max(srcCol, destCol);
        for (int col = startCol; col < endCol; col++) {
            Place position = new Place(move.getSource().getRow(), col);
            if (game.getPiece(position) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Vertical move
        int startRow = Math.min(srcRow, destRow) + 1;
        int endRow = Math.max(srcRow, destRow);
        for (int row = startRow; row < endRow; row++) {
            Place position = new Place(row, move.getSource().getCol());
            if (game.getPiece(position) != null) {
                countPiecesBetween++;
            }
        }
    }

    boolean isDestinationOccupied = game.getPiece(move.getDestination()) != null;

    if (isDestinationOccupied) {
        // Capture move: must jump over exactly one piece
        return countPiecesBetween == 1;
    } else {
        // Normal move: path must be clear

The `validate` method is intended to check whether a move involving a Knight piece is valid according to specific rules. Since the current implementation returns `true` if the piece is not a Knight, the main logic should handle Knight-specific move validation, typically involving the L-shaped move pattern of a Knight in chess.

Here's a complete implementation of the `validate` method that checks if the move is a valid Knight move (i.e., moving in an L-shape: two squares in one direction and one in the perpendicular direction):

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }

    int sourceRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int sourceCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int targetRow = move.getTarget().getRow();
    int targetCol = move.getTarget().getCol();

    int rowDiff = Math.abs(targetRow - sourceRow);
    int colDiff = Math.abs(targetCol - sourceCol);

    // Knight moves in an L-shape: (2,1) or (1,2)
    return (rowDiff == 2 && colDiff == 1) || (rowDiff == 1 && colDiff == 2);
}
```

This implementation calculates the difference in row and column positions between the source and target squares and verifies if the move conforms to the Knight's L-shaped movement pattern.

Response Text:---
The blocking rule for a Knight in Chinese chess (Xiangqi) states that the Knight's movement can be blocked if the "leg" position (the square immediately adjacent in the direction of movement) is occupied. To implement this, we need to:

1. Determine the move's source and target positions.
2. Identify the "leg" position based on the move's direction.
3. Check if the "leg" position is occupied by any piece.
4. Return false if blocked; otherwise, true.

Here's a complete implementation of the `validate` method:

```java
@Override
public boolean validate(Game game, Move move) {
    if (!(game.getPiece(move.getSource()) instanceof Knight)) {
        return true;
    }

    int sourceRow = move.getSource().getRow();
    int sourceCol = move.getSource().getCol();
    int targetRow = move.getTarget().getRow();
    int targetCol = move.getTarget().getCol();

    int rowDiff = targetRow - sourceRow;
    int colDiff = targetCol - sourceCol;

    // Check for L-shaped move: 2 in one direction and 1 in the other
    if (!((Math.abs(rowDiff) == 2 && Math.abs(colDiff) == 1) ||
          (Math.abs(rowDiff) == 1 && Math.abs(colDiff) == 2))) {
        return true; // Not a Knight move, so no blocking concern
    }

    // Determine the "leg" position that could block the Knight
    int legRow = sourceRow + (rowDiff == 2 ? 1 : (rowDiff == -2 ? -1 : 0));
    int legCol = sourceCol + (colDiff == 2 ? 1 : (colDiff == -2 ? -1 : 0));

    // Check if the "leg" position is occupied
    if (game.getPiece(new Place(legRow, legCol)) != null) {
        return false; // Move is blocked
    }

    return true; // Move is valid (not blocked)
}

    if (!((Math.abs(rowDiff) == 2 && Math.abs(colDiff) == 1) ||
          (Math.abs(rowDiff) == 1 && Math.abs(colDiff) == 2))) {
        return true; // Not a Knight move, so no blocking concern
    }

    // Determine the "leg" position that could block the Knight
    int legRow = sourceRow + (rowDiff == 2 ? 1 : (rowDiff == -2 ? -1 : 0));
    int legCol = sourceCol + (colDiff == 2 ? 1 : (colDiff == -2 ? -1 : 0));

    // Check if the "leg" position is occupied
    if (game.getPiece(new Place(legRow, legCol)) != null) {
        return false; // Move is blocked
    }

    return true; // Move is valid (not blocked)

```java
@Override
public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
    Scanner scanner = new Scanner(System.in);
    while (true) {
        System.out.print("Enter your move (e.g., a1->b3): ");
        String input = scanner.nextLine().trim();
        Move move = parseMove(input);
        if (move == null) {
            System.out.println("Invalid format. Please try again.");
            continue;
        }
        boolean isValid = false;
        for (Move availableMove : availableMoves) {
            if (move.equals(availableMove)) {
                isValid = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if (!isValid) {
            System.out.println("Move not available. Please choose a valid move.");
            continue;
        }
        String validationMsg = validateMove(game, move);
        if (validationMsg != null) {
            System.out.println("Invalid move: " + validationMsg);
            continue;
        }
        return move;
    }
}

import assignment.protocol.Game;

import assignment.protocol.Place;
import assignment.protocol.Player;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;

/**
 * The player that makes move according to user input from console.
 */
public class ConsolePlayer extends Player {
	public ConsolePlayer(String name, Color color) {
		super(name, color);
	}

	public ConsolePlayer(String name) {
		this(name, Color.GREEN);
	}

	/**
	 * Choose a move from available moves.
	 * This method will be called by {@link Game} object to get the move that the player wants to make when it is the
	 * player's turn.
	 * <p>
	 * {@link ConsolePlayer} returns a move according to user's input in the console.
	 * The console input format should conform the format described in the assignment description.
	 * (e.g. {@literal a1->b3} means move the {@link Piece} at {@link Place}(x=0,y=0) to {@link Place}(x=1,y=2))
	 * Note that in the {@link Game}.board, the index starts from 0 in both x and y dimension, while in the console
	 * display, x dimension index starts from 'a' and y dimension index starts from 1.
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: be sure to handle invalid input to avoid invalid {@link Move}s.
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: Student should make sure the {@link Move} returned is valid.</strong>
	 * <p>
	 * <strong>Attention: {@link Place} object uses integer as index of x and y-axis, both starting from 0 to
	 * facilitate programming.
	 * This is VERY different from the coordinate used in console display.</strong>
	 *
	 * @param game           the current game object
	 * @param availableMoves available moves for this player to choose from.
	 * @return the chosen move
	 */
	@Override
	public Move nextMove(Game game, Move[] availableMoves) {
		// TODO student implementation
		return availableMoves[0];
	}

	private String validateMove(Game game, Move move) {
		var rules = new Rule[] { new OutOfBoundaryRule(), new OccupiedRule(), new VacantRule(), new NilMoveRule(),
				new FirstNMovesProtectionRule(game.getConfiguration().getNumMovesProtection()), new ArcherMoveRule(),
				new KnightMoveRule(), new KnightBlockRule(), };
		for (var rule : rules) {
			if (!rule.validate(game, move)) {
				return rule.getDescription();
			}

			var piece = game.getPiece(move.getSource());
			if (piece == null) {
				return "No piece at " + move.getSource().toString();
			}
			if (!this.equals(piece.getPlayer())) {
				return "Cannot move a piece not belonging to you";
			}
		}
		return null;
	}

	private static Place parsePlace(String str) {
		if (str.length() < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		try {
			var x = str.charAt(0) - 'a';
			var y = Integer.parseInt(str.substring(1)) - 1;
			return new Place(x, y);
		} catch (NumberFormatException e) {
			return null;
		}
	}

	private static Move parseMove(String str) {
		var segments = str.split("->");
		if (segments.length < 2) {
			return null;
		}
		var source = parsePlace(segments[0].strip());
		if (source == null) {
			return null;
		}
		var destination = parsePlace(segments[1].strip());
		if (destination == null) {
			return null;
		}
		return new Move(source, destination);
	}
}

	 * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
	 * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position of the player.
	 * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
	 * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
	 * moving.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
		final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
		Position lastValidPosition = position;
		do {
			final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
			if (newPosition == null) {
				break;
			}

			lastValidPosition = newPosition;

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof StopCell) {
				break;
			}

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
					return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
				}

				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
					collectedGems.add(newPosition);
				} else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
					collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
				}
			}
		} while (true);

		if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
			return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
		}

		return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
	}

	/**

	 *
	 * @param position  The original position.
	 * @param direction The direction to offset.
	 * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
	 * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
				gameBoard.getNumCols());

		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Hint: Undoing a move is effectively the same as reversing everything you have done to make a move.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param prevMove The {@link MoveResult} object to revert.

	/**
	 * Tries to move the player from a position in the specified direction as far as possible.
	 *
	 * <p>
	 * Note that this method does <b>NOT</b> actually move the player. It just tries to move the player and return
	 * the state of the player as-if it has been moved.
	 * </p>
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position of the player.
	 * @param direction The direction to move the player in.
	 * @return An instance of {@link MoveResult} representing the type of the move and the position of the player after
	 * moving.
	 */
	@NotNull
	private MoveResult tryMove(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var collectedGems = new ArrayList<Position>();
		final var collectedExtraLives = new ArrayList<Position>();
		Position lastValidPosition = position;
		do {
			final Position newPosition = offsetPosition(lastValidPosition, direction);
			if (newPosition == null) {
				break;
			}

			lastValidPosition = newPosition;

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof StopCell) {
				break;
			}

			if (gameBoard.getCell(newPosition) instanceof EntityCell entityCell) {
				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Mine) {
					return new MoveResult.Valid.Dead(position, newPosition);
				}

				if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof Gem) {
					collectedGems.add(newPosition);
				} else if (entityCell.getEntity() instanceof ExtraLife) {
					collectedExtraLives.add(newPosition);
				}
			}
		} while (true);

		if (lastValidPosition.equals(position)) {
			return new MoveResult.Invalid(position);
		}

		return new MoveResult.Valid.Alive(lastValidPosition, position, collectedGems, collectedExtraLives);
	}

	/**
	 * Offsets the {@link Position} in the specified {@link Direction} by one step.
	 *
	 * @param position  The original position.
	 * @param direction The direction to offset.
	 * @return The given position offset by one in the specified direction. If the new position is outside of the game
	 * board, or contains a non-{@link EntityCell}, returns {@code null}.
	 */
	@Nullable
	private Position offsetPosition(@NotNull final Position position, @NotNull final Direction direction) {
		Objects.requireNonNull(position);
		Objects.requireNonNull(direction);

		final var newPos = position.offsetByOrNull(direction.getOffset(), gameBoard.getNumRows(),
				gameBoard.getNumCols());

		if (newPos == null) {
			return null;
		}
		if (!(gameBoard.getCell(newPos) instanceof EntityCell)) {
			return null;
		}

		return newPos;
	}

	public void GameBoardController(final GameBoard gameBoard) {
		this.gameBoard = Objects.requireNonNull(gameBoard, "gameBoard must not be null");
	}
}

        return;
    }

}

Here's the corrected `Entity` class with the appropriate constructor:

```java
package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * An entity on the game board.
 */
public abstract class Entity implements BoardElement {

    @Nullable
    private EntityCell owner;

    /**
     * Default constructor initializing owner to null.
     */
    public Entity() {
        this.owner = null;
    }

    /**
     * Constructor initializing owner with the given EntityCell.
     * @param owner the EntityCell to set as owner
     */
    public Entity(@Nullable EntityCell owner) {
        this.owner = owner;
    }

    /**
     * @return The {@link EntityCell} owning this entity, or {@code null} if this entity is not bound to a cell.
     */
    public final EntityCell getOwner() {
        return this.owner;
    }

    protected void Entity() {
        this.owner = null;
    }

    protected void Entity(final EntityCell owner) {
        this.owner = owner;
    }

    public final EntityCell setOwner(final EntityCell owner) {
        EntityCell previousOwner = this.owner;
        this.owner = owner;
        return previousOwner;
    }
}
```

Response Text:---
The `setEntity` method needs to perform ownership transfer logic:

1. Save the current entity (if any) to return later.
2. If there is an existing entity in the cell, unset its owner and clear its cell reference.
3. If the new entity is not null, unset its previous owner's reference (if any), set its owner to this cell, and update the cell's entity reference.
4. Return the previous entity.

Here's the complete implementation:

```java
public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
    Entity previousEntity = this.entity;

    // Unset owner of the previous entity if it exists
    if (previousEntity != null) {
        previousEntity.setOwner(null);
    }

    // If the new entity is not null, transfer ownership
    if (newEntity != null) {
        // Unset the previous owner of the new entity, if any
        Entity previousOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
        if (previousOwner != null && previousOwner != this) {
            previousOwner.setEntity(null);
        }
        // Set the owner of the new entity to this cell
        newEntity.setOwner(this);
    }

    // Set the new entity in this cell
    this.entity = newEntity;

    return previousEntity;
}

    Entity previousEntity = this.entity;

    // Unset owner of the previous entity if it exists
    if (previousEntity != null) {
        previousEntity.setOwner(null);
    }

    // If the new entity is not null, transfer ownership
    if (newEntity != null) {
        // Unset the previous owner of the new entity, if any
        Entity previousOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
        if (previousOwner != null && previousOwner != this) {
            previousOwner.setEntity(null);
        }
        // Set the owner of the new entity to this cell
        newEntity.setOwner(this);
    }

    // Set the new entity in this cell
    this.entity = newEntity;

    return previousEntity;
}

package pa1.model;

import org.jetbrains.annotations.NotNull;
import org.jetbrains.annotations.Nullable;

/**
 * A {@link Cell} on the game board which can contain an {@link Entity}.
 *
 * <p>
 * This class should observe and enforce the following constraints:
 * </p>
 * <ul>
 *     <li>There must be at most one entity owned by each cell; In other words, there should never be two entities'
 *     {@link Entity#getOwner()} pointing to the same {@link EntityCell}.</li>
 *     <li>There must be at most one cell owning each entity; In other words, there should never be two cells'
 *     {@link EntityCell#getEntity()} pointing to the same {@link Entity}.</li>
 * </ul>
 * <p>
 * More information is provided in the Javadoc of the methods in this class.
 * </p>
 */
public class EntityCell extends Cell {

	/**
	 * The entity which resides on this cell.
	 */
	@Nullable
	Entity entity = null;

	/**
	 * @return The entity currently present in this cell, or {@code null} if there is no entity present.
	 */
	public final Entity getEntity() {
		// TODO
		return null;
	}

	@Override
	public char toUnicodeChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toUnicodeChar() : '.';
	}

	@Override
	public char toASCIIChar() {
		return getEntity() != null ? getEntity().toASCIIChar() : '.';
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position) {
		super(position);
	}

	public void EntityCell(final Position position, final Entity initialEntity) {
		super(position);
		this.entity = initialEntity;
		if (initialEntity != null) {
			Entity previousOwner = initialEntity.getOwner();
			if (previousOwner != null && previousOwner != this) {
				previousOwner.setEntity(null);
			}
			initialEntity.setOwner(this);
		}
	}

	public Entity setEntity(final Entity newEntity) {
		Entity previousEntity = this.entity;
		if (previousEntity != null) {
			previousEntity.setOwner(null);
		}
		if (newEntity != null) {
			Entity previousOwner = newEntity.getOwner();
			if (previousOwner != null && previousOwner != this) {
				previousOwner.setEntity(null);
			}
			newEntity.setOwner(this);
		}
		this.entity = newEntity;
		return previousEntity;
	}
}

Response Text:---
The errors indicate that the code attempts to instantiate EntityCell objects using constructors like `new EntityCell(Position)` or `new EntityCell(Position, EntityType)` which are not defined in the EntityCell class. This suggests that EntityCell does not have such constructors, or they are not accessible.

**Explanation:**  
In the provided EntityCell class, the only constructor explicitly defined is the default constructor (implicit or explicit), and the `setEntity` method. There are no constructors accepting parameters like `Position` or `Entity`. Therefore, attempts to instantiate EntityCell with parameters will cause compilation errors.

**Solution:**  
Use the existing constructor (likely the default constructor) and then set properties via setter methods or direct field access if accessible. For example, instead of `new EntityCell(Position, Entity)`, create an EntityCell with `new EntityCell()` and then call `setPosition()` and `setEntity()` as needed.

**Corrected code snippet for creating an EntityCell with position and entity:**

```java
public Entity createEntityCell(Position position, Entity entity) {
    EntityCell cell = new EntityCell();
    cell.setPosition(position);
    cell.setEntity(entity);
    return cell;
}
```

**Note:**  
- Ensure that `setPosition()` and `setEntity()` methods exist in EntityCell. If not, you may need to modify EntityCell to include such setters or set fields directly if they are accessible.  
- Replace all instantiations like `new EntityCell(Position, Entity)` with this pattern throughout your codebase.

This approach aligns with the existing class design and resolves the compilation errors related to constructors.
